title: Eval Sentry: adaptive decisioning for gradual config/model flips with automated mitigation
creator: Priya Nandakumar
description:
Purpose: Implement an "eval-sentry" decisioning component that performs adaptive quality checks during gradual config or model flips (canary and A/B). The sentry should synthesize multiple signals (quality metrics, latency regressions, token-efficiency, and customer error-rate) and execute mitigation actions (pause, rollback, throttle, or route to fallback model) automatically according to a policy.

Key goals:
- Reduce mean time-to-detect and mean time-to-mitigate regressions during staged rollouts.
- Provide explainable reasons for automated decisions so PM/Support can audit rollouts.
- Minimize false positives by using baseline variance and cohort-aware thresholds.

Scope in this ticket:
- Evaluation policy engine: configurable rules combining absolute thresholds, relative-delta checks against baseline, and ensemble voting across metrics.
- Adaptive thresholds: use rolling-window variance from baseline cohorts to widen/narrow sensitivity per-metric.
- Mitigation actions: pause rollout, cut traffic to previous model variant, fall back to a cheaper compatible model, or throttle exposure.
- Dry-run and simulated-replay mode for validation against historical traffic.
- Integrations: rollout controller API, Console diagnostic page (links to example dashboard), BigQuery logging of decisions, and GitHub PR hooks for rollout metadata.
- Safety: ensure all actions are idempotent and reversible; include human approval path for P0 customer incidents.

Out of scope for this ticket: long-term ML-based anomaly detection (will follow), full support for on-prem private deployments (follow-up), and UI polish for Console diagnostics (minimal UI only).
acceptance_criteria: Eval-sentry service deployed behind feature flag in staging and canary clusters
Policy engine supports at least 3 metric types (generation quality, latency p95, error-rate) and evaluates ensemble voting rules
Automated mitigation actions executed and logged (pause, rollback, throttle) with idempotency tests
Dry-run mode produces identical decision logs without changing traffic; simulated-replay validates on two historical incidents
Console diagnostic page shows decision provenance and links to the evidence (metric deltas and sample prompts)
updates: 2025-01-12: Kickoff sync led by Rafael. PM Priya provided primary acceptance criteria. Agreed on use of ensemble voting to reduce single-metric flip sensitivity.

2025-01-17: Design review with Observability team. Decided to stream decision logs to BigQuery and also emit structured events to the existing rollout-trace topic (see design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/Eval+Sentry+Design).

2025-01-22: Spike complete: implemented prototype policy engine evaluating relative-delta and absolute thresholds; ran replay on two recent canary regressions and reproduced expected mitigations. Spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-safety/pull/321

2025-01-28: Safety review: added idempotency guard and human-approval exception for customers with active P0 incidents. Security flagged log retention for sensitive prompt samples—redaction plan added.

2025-02-02: Integration tests passing in staging. Starting gradual rollout behind feature flag to 2% traffic for internal teams. Observability dashboards: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/eval-sentry-canary
implementation_notes: Architecture: lightweight microservice written in Go, exposes /evaluate and /act endpoints and a read-only /dry-run mode
Policy format: JSON schema supporting boolean logic, comparator (<, >, delta_pct), and weighting for ensemble voting
Thresholds: default per-metric baseline + 3*stdev window; provide per-customer override for enterprise customers
Testing: create synthetic cohorts with injected regressions for automated test harness; add integration tests that validate rollback events in Kafka
Observability: emit decision events with fields [timestamp, rollout_id, cohort_id, metrics_snapshot, decision, evidence_refs]
risks: Risk: noisy metrics could cause oscillation between pause/rollback and resume. Mitigation: enforce minimum cool-down and require multi-window confirmation for rolling changes.
Risk: false positives impacting SLAs for large customers. Mitigation: provide enterprise opt-outs and human approval path; run extended dry-run on mirror traffic before full rollout.
Risk: exposure of prompt content in logs. Mitigation: implement redaction and hashing for sensitive fields and limit sample retention to 7 days by default.
